topic.title: Task-Relevant Representations and World Models for Control
topic.overview: Reinforcement learning often depends on representations or predictive models learned from complex observations. This topic asks what information these models should retain for effective action. Goal-aware prediction illustrates the issue: reconstructing every visual detail can waste capacity, so a model instead learns to emphasize quantities relevant to a specified goal.
topic.whyItMatters: A visually accurate prediction is not necessarily useful for planning. Aligning representation learning with downstream decisions can improve transfer and sample efficiency, especially when raw observations contain much more detail than a controller needs.
topic.evolution: The representatives extend from percept-to-action mappings and cross-domain transfer to state abstractions, video pretraining, and language-based dynamics. Recent work uses reinforcement learning to improve interactive video world models, evaluating both action-following accuracy and visual quality rather than treating appearance as sufficient.
openQuestions: How can task-focused representations retain information needed by unfamiliar future goals?
What evaluation reveals long-horizon control errors that short-term prediction metrics miss?
